name: application-anchor-scroll-nav
title: Anchor Scroll Nav
description: Sticky in-page section list with a left indicator bar on the currently active heading, for scrollspy-style page navigation.
useWhen: A long single-page document or article has multiple headings users may want to jump between.
You want the nav to reflect scroll position automatically, not just act as static jump links.
The page has enough vertical space for a persistent sidebar list, such as documentation layouts.
avoidWhen: The page is short enough that scrolling to a section is trivial — a table of contents adds more noise than value.
Navigation should switch between separate views rather than scroll within one page — use tabs instead.
You need this on narrow/mobile viewports where a persistent sidebar doesn't fit — collapse it into a dropdown or drawer there instead.
responsiveBehavior: The nav is a fixed w-48 column intended for a sidebar rail; hide or collapse it into a dropdown below your chosen mobile breakpoint.
accessibility: The active section link carries aria-current="location", the correct token for identifying an in-page current-location link.
The list uses semantic <nav> and <ul>/<li> so screen reader users can navigate it as a landmark and list.
Active state is shown with both a border color and font weight change, not color alone.

variants.title: Anchor scroll nav
variants.description: Five-item section list with a left border indicator on the active 'Overview' item.
accessibility: aria-current="location" is set only on the active item, updated as scroll position changes.

variants.title: Anchor scroll nav (Dark)
variants.description: Anchor scroll nav adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Active indicator and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
